answer: Land-Anchor Identity uses cadastral records to bind each agent ID to a distinct physical parcel. Registration requires a notarized parcel survey plus a copper wire loop installed on-site and read by a utility meter. Duplicate claims on one orchard parcel fail cross-checks against the county plot map; every ID near a shared knoll or boundary gets flagged. An attacker must acquire, survey, and meter each separate plot, costing thousands per identity and exposing land titles.
